Scope: phase 1 of the logistics area. Wet networks (sewerage, storm, potable water, fire fighting and TSE, including the force main), dry networks (medium voltage, low voltage, street lighting and telecom), the potable water pump station, the sewage lift station, guard rooms, all road layers up to the asphalt wearing course, and landscape.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 27-Oct-2026 data date the project is 60.7% complete against 76.0% planned, 15.3% behind the plan (SPI 0.80). It gained 2.8% this week against 4.9% planned, so the gap widened from 13.2% to 15.3%.

With 82.8% of the contract time gone, 39.3% of the work remains. Finishing by the contract completion date of 29-Jan-2027 needs about 3.0% a week over the 13 whole weeks left, against 2.8% achieved this week. The weekly report's milestone sheet and the P6 update now forecast project handover on 08-Mar-2027, 38 days late, a week later than last week's forecast. Construction is the weak phase: 50.0% done against 78.2% planned.

Telecom ducts and wet networks moved mostTelecom ducts rose by 4,362 LM to 60.8%, street-light cable by 1,791 LM to 23.2%, and fire-fighting pipes by 378 LM to 96.4%. Storm pipes are 95.2% installed, sewer pipes 89.9% and potable water pipes 82.0%.

The P6 update finishes the project on 08-Mar-2027, 38 days after the contract completion date. Every P6 milestone except telecom moved 7 days later, the same as the data date, so the update shows no recovery. The schedule has no finish constraint at the contract date, so its float is measured against its own late finish. The asphalt wearing course has only 5 days of float and construction finish 11 days. Other forecasts in this week's files: 21-Feb-2027 (General Information sheet), 20-Dec-2026 (recovery schedule in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet).

Procurement of key materials

Share of each long-lead item delivered to site. Source: weekly procurement update 27-Oct-2026. By discipline (Quality-Stat sheet), 114 of 155 materials are on site: civil and roads 61 of 77, electrical 22 of 30, mechanical 31 of 48.

Substations, RMUs and station panels not deliveredNone of the 3 unit substations or 5 RMUs is on site; both were due by 30-Oct-2026, "within 2 weeks of payment". The capacitor banks, MCCs and local control panels are due by 11-Nov-2026, and the PLC system and level meters by 19-Nov-2026. Planned delivery completion for electrical and mechanical materials was 27 and 28 Sep 2026.
Fire hydrants, valves and street-light cableOnly 13 of 82 fire hydrants are delivered, although the delivery date was 07-Jul-2026. Valves are at 61 of 121 and street-light cable at 6,054 of 20,000 LM, both due by 15-Nov-2026. The 3 surge tanks and the 2 cranes are due by 15 and 20 Nov 2026.

Data notes

  • Report week: the weekly report states "Current Contract Weeks: 65 of 78" (Milestones sheet). The report serial number (WPR 047) and the consultant's inspection number (47) are not the week number.
  • This-week values compare this report with the 20-Oct-2026 report (previous week folder). The 13-Oct S-curve row is derived from the 20-Oct report.
  • Four different completion forecasts: 21-Feb-2027 (General Information sheet, −23 days), 08-Mar-2027 (Milestones sheet and P6 update, −38 days), 20-Dec-2026 (recovery schedule in the progress presentation) and 30-Nov-2026 (look-ahead sheet and the presentation's "target" date).
  • The P6 update has no finish constraint, so no activity shows negative float although it finishes after the contract date. All milestones except telecom moved 7 days, the same as the data date. 215 in-progress activities have finish dates before the data date.
  • This week's Physical-Chart Data sheet lowers earlier monthly actuals (May 28.9% to 28.2%, July 40.1% to 39.4%, September 49.7% to 48.9%).
  • Quantities and man-hours disagree this week: Major Quantities adds 391 LM of MV cable, 440 LM of LV cable and 235 m³ of asphalt, but the MV, LV and road works packages earned no man-hours.
  • Mobilisation: the weekly report gives 30-Aug-2025 as actual, the P6 milestone "Mobilization - Finish" gives 25-Nov-2025.
  • The "Complete earthworks" forecast of 01-Sep-2026 has passed but is still marked as a forecast, with earthworks at 96.2%. The "all materials delivered" forecast of 31-Oct-2026 conflicts with 41 of 155 materials not yet on site.
  • The procurement log in the workbook is still unusable (delivered figures above quantities, #DIV/0! and #VALUE! cells, project ID DAM2-01-029), and the front-page procurement total still repeats the mechanical row. The procurement presentation lists 5 RMUs while the quantities and the MV slide give 3; it gives 377 street-light poles delivered against 380 on the lighting slide, and 13 fire hydrants against 12. It also has malformed dates (15/111/26, 31/09/2026).
  • NCRs: the front page shows 4 issued and 3 closed; the Quality-Stat sheet shows 51 issued and 50 closed.
  • Labour: the front page shows 360 planned and 483 actual; the Manpower sheet shows 78 planned and 537 actual for October.
  • Sewer quantities differ across the files: Major Quantities 6,803 of 7,567 LM (89.9%), the Conclusion sheet 6,803 of 6,146 LM (110.7%), and the presentation 6,135 of 6,257 LM (98.1%). Shop drawings: 1,774 approved in the workbook, 1,818 in the presentation.
  • Contract value is 198,906,162.61 on the front page and 198,906,162.312 "incl. VAT" in the Conclusion sheet. The invoice log has stray values (21,100,000, 20,900,000, 200,000) and EAC shows #REF!.
  • Key submittal dates are in Feb–Mar 2024, before the contract award of 30-Jun-2025. The look-ahead sheet contains P6 data from the Hail Industrial City Phase II project, and the risk register uses project ID DAM2-01-029 and names the 3rd and 6th Industrial Cities.
  • The workbook's issue 1 text still quotes 304 workers and 184 items of equipment; the presentation gives 537 workers and 304 items of equipment.
  • The workbook's front page and the presentation's acceleration plan also report cost-based progress; this report uses physical progress only.
